rag_hits.title: Flood Resilience at NYCHA — Lessons Learned
rag_hits.text: Letter from the Vice President for Recovery & Resilience Dear New Yorkers, Hurricane Sandy devasted New York City in October 2012. Despite living in a city with 520 miles of coastline, residents had never grappled with storm surge at this scale. Salt water and debris covered huge swaths of the five boroughs, including many NYCHA campuses. Unlike prior major storms, the impacts didn’t dissipate when the weather improved. Salt water corroded critical infrastructure that was stored below grade. The homes of tens of thousands of public housing residents—most of whom couldn’t evacuate before the storm—were without water, power, heat, hot water, or elevator service for weeks.

final.paragraph:
This is an automated hazard-exposure briefing produced by Riprap from live and precomputed data sources. It is informational only and not a substitute for a professional risk assessment.

**In brief.**
This address is outside the 2012 Sandy inundation footprint [sandy_inundation], in FEMA flood zone X (an area of minimal flood hazard) [fema_nfhl], and outside the modeled flooding in the DEP stormwater scenarios for current, 2050 and 2080 sea-level rise [dep_moderate_current][dep_moderate_2050][dep_extreme_2080]. 12 flood-related 311 complaints were filed within 200 m in the last 5 years [nyc311].

**Hazard Reader.**
This address sits outside the empirical 2012 Hurricane Sandy inundation footprint (NYC OEM) [sandy_inundation]. This address sits in FEMA flood zone X (an area of minimal flood hazard), per NFHL FIRM panel 3604970081F, effective 2007 [fema_nfhl]. FEMA's preliminary flood map (PFIRM issued 2015-01-30, community 360497) places this address in zone X (an area of minimal flood hazard). A preliminary map is not the effective map and does not set flood insurance [fema_pfirm]. NYC DEP stormwater scenarios at this address: current sea level with 2.13 in/hr of rain, outside the modeled flooding [dep_moderate_current]; 2050 sea-level rise with 2.13 in/hr, outside the modeled flooding [dep_moderate_2050]; 2080 sea-level rise with 3.66 in/hr, outside the modeled flooding [dep_extreme_2080]. USGS surveyed 4 Hurricane Ida high-water marks within 800 m of this address; the highest stood 1.95 ft above ground; the highest water surface elevation was 21.0 ft NAVD88 [ida_hwm]. Nearest mark: Northwest of intersection of Indian Rd. and West 218th St., at cut channel of the Harlem River, Inwood Hill Park, Manhattan (635 m away) [ida_hwm]. Experimental: a satellite model (Prithvi-EO 2.0, NYC fine-tune) on Sentinel-2 scenes from 2021-09-02, compared with 2021-08-13: 0 m² of new surface water within 500 m of this address (100% of that circle observed); 0.00% of Inwood showed new water (100% of it observed) [prithvi_water]. Street and basement flooding drains within hours and is not visible at 10 to 20 m, so no water here is not evidence of no flooding [prithvi_water]. Elevation 11.14 m; this point is higher than 50% of the ground within 200 m (the 50th percentile; a low percentile means a local low spot where water collects); HAND (height above the nearest drainage channel) 11.14 m; TWI (topographic wetness index; higher means water tends to collect) 6.26 [microtopo]. Local basin relief (the rise from this point to the highest ground within 750 m): 59.89 m [microtopo]. Experimental: Policy passages retrieved from the NYC flood-policy corpus for this place: 1 (embedding retrieval; entity tags are experimental) [policy_corpus].

**Live Observer.**
4 FloodNet community sensors within 600 m have logged 8 above-curb flood events in the last 3 years [floodnet]. Peak depth recorded by the sensors in good working order: 126 mm on 2025-10-30 [floodnet]. 12 NYC 311 flood-related complaints filed within 200 m of this location in the last 5 years: 10 catch basin, 2 sewer backup [nyc311]. Latest METAR at LaGuardia Airport, NY (10.4 km away): 23.0°C, observed 2026-09-30 20:35 UTC [nws_obs]. Latest reading at Kings Point, NY: 7.43 ft above MLLW (+0.87 ft vs predicted tide), observed 2026-09-30 20:42 UTC [noaa_tides].

**Asset Register.**
21 MTA subway entrances within 800 m of this address; of the nearest 8: 0 inside the 2012 Sandy inundation extent and 0 inside the DEP extreme stormwater scenario (2080 sea-level rise) [mta_entrance_exposure]. 0 flood-exposed NYCHA developments within 2000 m of this address (the register lists only developments found inside the 2012 Sandy extent or a DEP stormwater scenario, not every development): 0 inside the 2012 Sandy inundation extent and 0 inside the DEP extreme stormwater scenario (2080 sea-level rise) [nycha_development_exposure]. 1 flood-exposed NYC DOE school within 1500 m of this address (the register lists only schools found inside the 2012 Sandy extent or a DEP stormwater scenario, not every school): 0 inside the 2012 Sandy inundation extent and 1 inside the DEP extreme stormwater scenario (2080 sea-level rise) [doe_school_exposure]. 3 hospitals within 3000 m of this address: 0 inside the 2012 Sandy inundation extent and 0 inside the DEP extreme stormwater scenario (2080 sea-level rise) [doh_hospital_exposure].

**Projector.**
No active NWS flood, coastal or wind alerts at this point, checked 2026-09-30 20:51 UTC [nws_alerts]. Experimental: a TTM model fine-tuned on Battery gauge history, with no wind or pressure input, forecasts a peak surge residual of 0.22 m at The Battery about 63 h ahead; for storm decisions use NOAA ETSS or the Stevens Flood Advisory System instead [ttm_battery_surge]. Experimental: 4 flood-related 311 complaints within 200 m over the last 512 days; a zero-shot TTM forecast with no rainfall input and no backtest projects about 0.03 per week for the next 96 days [ttm_311_forecast]. NPCC4 (2024) projects sea-level rise at the Battery of 0.38 m (15 in) by the 2050s and 0.79 m (31 in) by 2100 at the median, relative to 2000-2004; 90th percentile 0.74 m and 1.65 m [npcc4_slr].

**Out of scope.** This briefing does not assess title, structural condition, or compliance with specific zoning rules. Where a probe was offline at run time, the relevant section omits that signal.
